current_contract_findings: build_plan is downstream archive-component planning. It requires real content hashes, target fingerprints and validated capability evidence. Provider relation IDs are neither archive component paths nor installed runtime capability IDs; translating them directly would fabricate authority.

The existing planner already has iterative deterministic graph traversal, SCC/cycle classification and blocked-dependent closure. Its exact/>= version constraints apply to declared capability requirements, not arbitrary Nexus file labels. They should not be invented from free-form notes, mod versions or file names.

Pinned v1 IFileInfo provides is_primary:bool, category_id:number and category_name:string. Native file_record currently drops all three. Category1/MAIN is the pinned main-file category; PATCH/OPTION/OLD_VERSION/DELETED/ARCHIVED are distinct. File version explicitly need not match mod version. Author-declared update links are not guaranteed to exist or form complete chains.

Normalized Requirements establishes complete mod-level discovery only. Internal identity is (game, canonical decimal mod_id). Distinct relation IDs targeting the same mod must preserve provenance while fetch/choice work is deduplicated by mod identity. External rows and DLC rows remain unresolved, never satisfied by a similarly named source archive.

Current native source jobs require explicit game/mod_id/file_id. They reject nxm and target_ref fields; no automatic prerequisite queue exists. Native resolver requires current premium entitlement or a bound unexpired structured website grant. Jobs currently cannot accept that free-account grant/resume route.

Current retained-source IoStore generation admits only1..8 selected successful same-domain downloads, verifies immutable source identity and refuses overlaps. A discovered cross-domain prerequisite or closure exceeding8 sources cannot silently enter this generation. Requirements do not define package winner/load ordering; no priority should be inferred from traversal.

recommended_bounded_increment.scope: One authenticated read-only prerequisite acquisition plan in the current provider/auth files, not a second runtime or generic manifest owner.
recommended_bounded_increment.file_selection: Extend file_record and its owning native report with strictly typed is_primary/category facts (unknown/missing restrictive). A pure bounded selector consumes complete live files plus a caller-declared policy: explicit file_id mapping wins only after exact membership/identity validation; automatic unique-current-primary may choose only one is_primary=true MAIN candidate with consistent known category facts. Zero/multiple/unknown candidates require explicit choice. Never choose by highest file_id, lexical version, timestamp, filename or notes. Selection is an acquisition candidate; required file/version constraints remain not_provided and installation false.
recommended_bounded_increment.recursive_auth_seam: Add an additive auth-owned plan C ABI beside mb_nexus_auth_catalog_v1. Reuse private catalog_request/requirements_request and visibility/adult checks under ONE Busy/Operation/borrowed cookie/token lifetime; calling the public catalog ABI recursively would hit Busy or reset the budget. Reuse CatalogWork scratch sequentially, deduplicate (game, numeric mod_id), and validate source identity/full discovery before adding edges. One remaining monotonic/cancel budget covers every request, selection, rendering and cleanup.
recommended_bounded_increment.bounds: Initially cap the complete internal-mod closure at8 (including roots) to match current source/generation capacity; bound edge/external/DLC totals and report bytes explicitly. Requests for child mod_id>INT32_MAX remain unresolved because the fixed GraphQL query uses Int, although decoder preserves signed63 identities. Process a stable identity order; cycle/hidden/incomplete/limit/transport failures produce typed unresolved reasons without claiming a complete ready acquisition set.
recommended_bounded_increment.graph_semantics: Return deterministic prerequisite-first selected sources and original typed relations, preserving missing choices/external/DLC/cross-domain causes. Required-mod relations do not assert load order. Treat recursive cycles as unresolved absent a separately justified co-acquisition policy. Reuse existing graph semantics where appropriate; do not feed fabricated hashes/validated capabilities into build_plan before downloads.
recommended_bounded_increment.app_integration: Expose the plan through existing bounded native HTTP/auth routing, using explicit roots/file choices/selection policy; no new UI required. It initially performs metadata planning only. A later job coordinator can consume fully bound chosen game/mod/file identities through the existing auth resolver and source job idempotency, then supply only successful original job IDs to the existing generation contract. Do not remove analysis missing_requirements or infer auto-install from metadata success.

file_schema_scope.official_scope: Pinned v1 IFileInfo (not v3 unique version IDs): is_primary:boolean, category_id:number, category_name:string, file_id:number, version:string.
file_schema_scope.automatic_policy_candidate: Only is_primary=true AND category_id=1 AND category_name=MAIN. Missing/wrong-type/unknown or contradictory facts remain unresolved; zero or multiple candidates/duplicate IDs remain unresolved. Never select an archived/deleted/old/patch/optional row under current-primary policy, even if its primary flag is true.
file_schema_scope.selection_vs_satisfaction: Chosen game/mod/file identity is selected_by_declared_policy only. Keep file_version_constraints_provided=false, compatibility/version satisfaction unresolved and installation_supported=false. Absence of a version/file requirement is not proof of compatibility or installed satisfaction. An explicit historical file choice is separately recorded, cannot become a current-primary choice or compatibility proof.

focused_proof_for_implementation: Actual decoder+selector: primary MAIN choice independent of file order; explicit exact choice; missing flags, duplicate identities or multiple primary candidates unresolved; distinct file/mod version labels never converted into constraints.

Owned TLS recursive graph: diamond fetches each identity once; hidden child makes no requirements POST; cycles, >INT32 child IDs, closure cap, partial response and cancellation revoke completeness and publish no ready prefix.

Actual native HTTP plan reports chosen typed sources plus external/DLC/cross-domain unresolved facts, with no provider credentials/signed links/installation assertion. Normal resolver still independently enforces current account/grant authority before downloads.
uncertainty: Pinned SDK declarations establish field meaning, not live-account acceptance or actual provider prevalence/uniqueness of primary/category flags. Unknown fields must be restrictive.
Mod-level prerequisites lack exact file/version constraints; deterministic policy can select a candidate, but cannot establish undocumented compatibility or installed status.
Existing single/generation public routes do not yet own a recursive plan-to-queue transaction or free-account per-prerequisite website-grant handoff.
